note.clockOnOscillator: Clock port {{port}} takes the board's {{mhz}} MHz oscillator (pin {{pin}}); it is not mapped.
note.outOfResources: "{{name}}": the board has no free resource left for {{count}} of its pins; map them by hand or leave them open / constant.
note.rgbOnLeds: RGB LED "{{name}}": the board has no free RGB LED, so red, green and blue went to single LEDs.
note.hexDigitOnLeds: Hex digit "{{name}}": its 4-bit value and dot went to LEDs; to see the digit on a 7-segment display, decode it in the circuit (a hex to 7-segment decoder) and map the segments.
note.powerOnResetOnButton: Power-on reset "{{name}}" went to a button: for a real power-on pulse use the board's reset circuit, or a counter on the board clock.
note.portIoConnector: Port I/O "{{name}}" has bidirectional (three-state) pins: they went to connector pins (Pmod / GPIO); check that the connector is the one you wire.
note.partActiveLow: "{{name}}" is set to light on 0: its port carries the circuit's value and the board's own active level is handled for you, so on the board it lights the other way round. Set the part to light on 1 for the same picture.

noResource.programmableGenerator: Programmable generator "{{name}}": a board has no such waveform source; build it with a counter / state machine on the board clock, or map the port to an outside signal by hand.
noResource.matrixKeypad: Keypad "{{name}}": its row and column ports go to an outside keypad such as a Pmod KYPD; map them to connector pins by hand (the columns need pull-ups).
noResource.joystick: Joystick "{{name}}": the board has no joystick; map X / Y to the digital output of an outside joystick / ADC, or to switches, by hand.
noResource.realTimeClock: Real-time clock "{{name}}": an FPGA has no wall clock; give the value from an outside RTC or from a counter on the board clock.
noResource.evoBuzzer: Buzzer "{{name}}": its ports (frequency, enable, volume, duty cycle) make no sound on the pins themselves; connect them to a tone (PWM) generator on the board clock or an audio codec and map its output to the board's audio / buzzer pin.
noResource.buzzer: Buzzer "{{name}}": connect its enable and note ports to a tone (PWM) generator on the board clock and map its output to the board's audio / buzzer pin.
noResource.digitalOscilloscope: Digital oscilloscope "{{name}}": its ports (CLK, inputs, EN, CLR) are not a display on the board; watch them with the FPGA's built-in logic analyzer (Xilinx ILA, Intel SignalTap) or map them by hand to pins going to an outside logic analyzer.
noResource.keyboard: Keyboard "{{name}}": the board has none; connect OUT / AV to the output of a UART or PS/2 receiver and RE / CK / CLR to it (or map them to connector pins by hand).
noResource.asciiKeyboard: ASCII keyboard "{{name}}": the board has none; give the data and strobe ports from a UART or PS/2 receiver (or map them to connector pins by hand).
noResource.tty: Text terminal "{{name}}": the board has none; connect IN / WE / CK / CLR to a UART transmitter or a VGA text controller (or map them to connector pins by hand).
noResource.telnet: Telnet "{{name}}": the network link needs a UART bridge or an Ethernet core; connect OUT / AV / IN / WR / RD / CK to it.
noResource.rgbVideo: RGB video "{{name}}": connect RST / CK / WE / X / Y / DATA to a VGA / HDMI controller that writes a frame buffer (the board's VGA pins cannot be driven directly), or map them to connector pins by hand.
noResource.dotMatrix: Dot matrix "{{name}}": its row / column ports are left for you to map, on an LED array or on connector pins.

drc.otherBoard: The mapping was made for board {{mapped}}, not for {{board}}.
drc.staleParts: The mapping still has {{count}} part(s) that are no longer in the circuit; they are ignored.
drc.widthChanged: "{{name}}" changed from {{was}} to {{now}} pins since it was mapped; map it again.
drc.unmapped: "{{name}}": {{count}} of its {{total}} pins are not mapped (map them, or leave outputs open and inputs at a constant).
drc.openInput: {{pin}} is an input: it cannot be left open, give it a constant 0 or 1 instead.
drc.constOnOutput: {{pin}} is an output: it cannot take a constant, leave it open instead.
drc.unknownResource: {{pin}} is mapped on a resource at {{resource}} that the board does not have.
drc.mappedOnZeroPinResource: {{pin}} is mapped on "{{resource}}", which has no FPGA pin on this board.
drc.pinOutOfRange: {{pin}} is mapped on pin {{index}} of "{{resource}}", which has only {{count}}.

in.out: {{pin}} is an input of the circuit but "{{resource}}" is an output of the board (an LED, a display ...).

out.in: {{pin}} is an output of the circuit but "{{resource}}" is an input of the board (a button, a switch ...).

inout.in: {{pin}} is bidirectional but "{{resource}}" can only be read; map it on bidirectional (connector) pins.
inout.out: {{pin}} is bidirectional but "{{resource}}" can only be driven; map it on bidirectional (connector) pins.

drc.clockPinUsed: {{pin}} is mapped on FPGA pin {{fpgaPin}}, the board's clock pin.
drc.pinUsedTwice: One pin of "{{resource}}" is mapped twice: {{pins}}.
drc.fpgaPinShared: FPGA pin {{fpgaPin}} is used by more than one board resource: {{resources}}.
drc.unsafeBoardText: The board file has an FPGA pin or device name the pin constraint files cannot take safely: {{text}}. Use only letters, digits and '_' in pin names (and also spaces, '.' and '-' in the part, family and package).
drc.zeroPinResource: The board resource "{{resource}}" has no FPGA pin and cannot be used.
drc.topLevelNoIo: The circuit has no inputs or outputs, so there is nothing to put on the board.
drc.noLabel: The part behind port {{port}} has no label of its own; it gets one when the board map is saved for Logisim-evolution (which needs it). Give it a label to choose the name yourself.
drc.labelChar: Label "{{label}}" has the character '{{char}}', which an HDL name cannot have; the port is called {{port}}, and Logisim-evolution will not accept the label.

label.vhdlKeyword: Label "{{label}}" is a VHDL keyword; the port is called {{port}}, and Logisim-evolution will not accept the label.
label.verilogKeyword: Label "{{label}}" is a Verilog keyword; the port is called {{port}}, and Logisim-evolution will not accept the label.

drc.duplicateLabel: Label "{{label}}" is used by more than one I/O part (also "{{other}}"; labels are compared without case); the board map cannot tell them apart.
drc.gatedClock: The clock of "{{part}}" goes through logic gates (a gated clock): on an FPGA this gives glitches and timing problems; use an enable input instead.
drc.clockFromLogic: The clock of "{{part}}" does not come from a clock part (a button, a switch or a flip-flop output drives it): on an FPGA, sample it with the board clock and use an enable instead.
drc.clockUnused: Clock "{{name}}" is not connected to anything.
drc.multipleClocks: The circuit has {{count}} clocks; each is made from the board oscillator.
drc.resourcePins: {{resource}} has {{actual}} FPGA pin(s), but its drive needs {{expected}}: fix the board file.

build.title: Build and program the board
build.intro: The circuit is turned into a bitstream for this board with the open-source toolchain (Yosys and nextpnr; ecppack for Lattice ECP5, openXC7 for Xilinx 7-series).
build.notSupported: There is no open-source flow for {{board}} yet; Lattice ECP5 (GECKO5) and Xilinx 7-series boards (Basys3, Nexys A7, PYNQ-Z2 ...) can be built. For other boards, download the project files and open them in the vendor tool.
build.unknownPart: The board's FPGA part ({{part}}) is not known to the open-source flow.
build.xc7Web: Xilinx 7-series boards ({{board}}) are built with openXC7, which runs only in the desktop app (there is no browser build of it). Download the project files from the "FPGA project" tab of the HDL window and build them with openXC7 or Vivado, or use the desktop app.
build.badPackage: The board's FPGA package ({{pkg}}) is not valid.
build.drcBlocked: The design check found {{count}} errors; fix them before building.
build.noMapping: The circuit is not mapped on a board yet; map it before building.
build.vhdlAsVerilog: GHDL does not run here, so the Verilog form of the same circuit is built instead of the VHDL.
build.cancelFlashBlocked: A flash write cannot be stopped halfway: the board would be left without a working design.
build.downloaded: {{file}} downloaded. Load it onto the board with your own programmer (e.g. openFPGALoader).
build.downloadFailed: The browser could not start the download.
build.stale: The circuit changed after the last build; build again before programming.

target.label: Target
target.sramTitle: The design is loaded into the FPGA's memory and is lost at power-off. Fast, and does not wear the flash.
target.flashTitle: The design is written to the board's configuration flash and loads at every power-on. The app asks before writing.
target.flashUnsupported: On a Zynq board the flash is written through the processor side; only SRAM loading is available here.

result.builtWeb: Bitstream ready ({{size}} KB, {{seconds}} s). The browser cannot write to the board; download the file and load it with your own programmer.
result.programmedSram: The design was loaded into the FPGA's SRAM; it runs until power-off.
result.programmedFlash: The design was written to the configuration flash; it loads at every power-on.
result.detected: Board found; details in the log.
result.declined: The write was not confirmed; nothing was written.
result.programmedCpld: The design was written into the CPLD; it keeps it after power-off.

program.noCable: No programming cable was found. Check that the board is plugged in over USB and that the driver is installed (on Windows, WinUSB/libusbK through Zadig).
program.noFpga: The cable answered but there is no FPGA on the JTAG chain. Check that the board is powered.
program.unknownBoard: This openFPGALoader version does not know the board name; install a newer version.
program.unknownCable: This openFPGALoader version does not know the board's cable; install a newer version.
program.wrongDevice: The bitstream is not for the connected FPGA (or openFPGALoader does not know that FPGA). Check that the right board is selected.
program.other: openFPGALoader ended with exit code {{code}}; details in the log.

error.stalled: The {{stage}} step printed nothing after it started and was stopped: the program hung while starting.

programVivado.noCable: Vivado's hw_server found no JTAG cable. Check that the board is plugged in over USB and that Vivado's cable drivers are installed (Vivado\data\xicom\cable_drivers\nt64\install_drivers.cmd, run as administrator). A cable whose driver was switched to WinUSB with Zadig (for openFPGALoader) is not seen by Vivado.
programVivado.noFpga: The JTAG cable answered but there is no FPGA on its chain. Check that the board is powered.
programVivado.wrongDevice: None of the connected JTAG chains holds this board's FPGA, or the bitstream is for another device. Check that the right board is selected and plugged in.
programVivado.other: Vivado ended programming with exit code {{code}}; details in the log.

programQuartus.noCable: quartus_pgm found no programming cable (Error 213013). Check that the board is plugged in over USB and that the USB-Blaster driver is installed (Device Manager: update the driver from the Quartus folder quartus\drivers\usb-blaster or usb-blaster-ii). A cable whose driver was switched to WinUSB with Zadig (for openFPGALoader) is not seen by Quartus.
programQuartus.noFpga: The cable answered but no device was found on its JTAG chain. Check that the board is powered.
programQuartus.wrongDevice: The device on the JTAG chain is not the one the file was built for. Check that the right board is selected and plugged in.
programQuartus.other: quartus_pgm ended with exit code {{code}}; details in the log.

programIse.noCable: iMPACT found no programming cable ("Cable autodetection failed"). Check that the board is plugged in over USB and that the Xilinx cable driver is installed (run install_drivers.exe from the ISE folder common\bin\nt64 as administrator). Digilent boards with an Adept USB port (Basys 2) need Digilent's iMPACT plug-in or Digilent Adept; you can also save the file and load it with Adept.
programIse.noFpga: The cable answered but no device was found on its JTAG chain. Check that the board is powered.
programIse.wrongDevice: The device at the board's JTAG position is not the one the file was built for. Check that the right board is selected and plugged in.
programIse.other: iMPACT ended with exit code {{code}}; details in the log.

error.vendorMissing: {{tool}} was not found on this computer.

vendorHint.vivadoLicense: Vivado did not find a valid license (exit code 42). Since 2026.1 even the free tier needs a license file: create one in AMD's license portal, save it as %USERPROFILE%\.Xilinx\Xilinx.lic (or set XILINXD_LICENSE_FILE to its path) and restart the app.
vendorHint.iseStartupHang: ISE hung while starting (no output at all). On Windows 10/11 this happens when a network provider blocks ISE's start-up scan, usually WSL's "P9NP" provider. Remove P9NP from the network provider order while you use ISE (HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\NetworkProvider\Order), then try again. A Windows or WSL update can add it back.
vendorHint.stalled: The vendor tool printed nothing after it started and was stopped. Start it once by hand to see whether it asks for something (a license, a first-run setup).
vendorHint.quartusFamilyLicense: This FPGA family needs a paid Quartus license: Quartus II 13.0sp1 Web Edition does not build for it (Error 20005). The free editions cannot build this board.
vendorHint.iseDeviceNotInWebpack: This FPGA is not in the free ISE WebPACK edition (Xst:1817, invalid target device). It needs a licensed ISE edition.
vendorHint.desktopOnly: Vivado, Quartus and ISE run only in the desktop app, with your installed vendor tool.
vendorHint.setFolder: Install it, or if it is already installed, choose its folder under "Vendor tools" at the bottom of this panel.
vendorHint.hwServerRunning: Vivado's hardware server is still running (hw_server.exe, cs_server.exe) and holds the JTAG cable, so openFPGALoader cannot use it. Vivado leaves it running after it closes: end hw_server.exe and cs_server.exe in Task Manager, then try again.
vendorHint.hwServerMaybe: If you used Vivado on this computer, its hardware server (hw_server.exe, cs_server.exe) may still be running and holding the JTAG cable: end both in Task Manager, then try again.

build.vivadoFlowNote: The open-source flow cannot build this board's FPGA, so it is built and programmed with your installed Vivado (programming loads the FPGA's SRAM; the design is lost at power-off).
build.quartusFlowNote: This board is built and programmed with your installed Quartus (Quartus II 13.0sp1 for Cyclone I-III and MAX 7000, Quartus Prime for the newer families). Programming loads the FPGA's SRAM through the first USB-Blaster; the design is lost at power-off.
build.quartusCpldNote: This board's CPLD is built and programmed with your installed Quartus. A CPLD has no SRAM load: programming writes the design into the chip for good (you are asked first), through the first USB-Blaster.
build.iseFlowNote: This board is built and programmed with your installed ISE 14.7 (WebPACK). Programming loads the FPGA's SRAM with iMPACT through the first Xilinx cable; the design is lost at power-off.
build.iseCpldNote: This board's CoolRunner-II CPLD is built and programmed with your installed ISE 14.7. A CPLD has no SRAM load: programming erases the chip and writes the design into it for good (you are asked first), through the first Xilinx cable.

vendorTools.title: Vendor tools
